metadata.note: William Edenborn's road: the Shreveport and Red River Valley Railway (1897-1903) and its successor the Louisiana Railway and Navigation Company (1903 until the Louisiana and Arkansas lease of 1928/29), Shreveport - Alexandria - Moreauville - Naples, car ferry to Angola, then the east bank through St. Francisville and Baton Rouge to New Orleans, with the Aloha - Winnfield branch and the 1923 Texas affiliate McKinney - Waskom. Drawn from the research report research/branches/louisiana_railway_and_navigation_company.txt (historical-trains repo, researched 2026-11-12) and converted 2026-11-12. Only the report's drawable spans are drawn. The S&RRV and the LR&N are separate corporations with separate colours (same owner; the 22 Jun 1903 sale is drawn as a change of company, overlapping in 1903). The LR&N of Texas carries the LR&N colour (same owner, same company for Rule 4). The Louisiana and Arkansas (1929-1939) and Kansas City Southern (1939-1969) eras on this track are NOT drawn here - they belong to the louisiana_and_arkansas_railway cycle.
sources: ICC valuation report, Louisiana Railway and Navigation Co. (Val. Rep. vol. 106), abstract: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:WikiProject_Trains/ICC_valuations/Louisiana_Railway_and_Navigation_Company

John Fowler, Louisiana Railroads - Passenger Stations & Stops (SL 248), tables 14, 15, 18, 21, 22: https://www.branchline.uk/jfpdf/louisianarrs.pdf ; Texas table 155: https://www.branchline.uk/jfpdf/texasrrs2.pdf

Chronicling America (loc.gov) OCR: Colfax Chronicle 29 Oct 1898, 24 Nov 1900; Bossier Banner 23 Sep 1897; Natchitoches Enterprise 30 Mar 1899; Southern Sentinel (Winnfield) 16 Nov 1906, 12 Apr 1907, 19 Apr 1907, 8 May 1908, 15 May 1908, 31 Jul 1908; Donaldsonville Chief 1 Dec 1906
metadata.not_yet_sourced: OPEN ENDS - these end years are the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end: Shreveport - Alexandria, Alexandria - Moreauville, Angola - Baton Rouge and Baton Rouge - New Orleans stop at 1923 (no LR&N timetable after 1922-23 found; the LR&N name lasted to the L&A lease, 1928 or 1929); Moreauville - Big Bend and Big Bend - Naples stop at 1922 (the 1922 timetable; never draw after the 1928 Torras re-route); the Winnfield Branch stops at 1908 (last card found). ANCHOR: the Texas line is drawn for 1926 only, the one year a source proves LR&N-name passenger service. UNRESOLVED: lease date 1928 vs 1929; whether the Simmesport rail bridge (and so the Torras route) dates from 1928 or about 1915, which would move the Naples route's end earlier; Alexandria - Mansura passenger service in 1903 (track complete, no train proven); local trains south of Moreauville before 14 Apr 1907; whether LR&N of Texas trains ran into Shreveport over the IC from the state line; Fowler's 'Louisiana Rly (LR)' tag on tables 18 and 21 read as LR&N shorthand. headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates throughout.
metadata.branches_deliberately_omitted: Alexandria - Mansura under the S&RRV name (track complete by Jun 1903, no S&RRV passenger evidence; drawn from 1904 as LR&N). The Mississippi car ferry Naples - Angola (Angola Transfer Co., not rail; nothing is drawn across the water, so the main line is discontinuous between Naples and Angola). Moreauville - Simmesport - Torras Jct - Filston (no LR&N-era passenger evidence; L&A-era from a 1930 Fowler sighting - for the L&A cycle). Waskom - Shreveport over the Illinois Central (LR&N of Texas use not confirmed). Tioga Branch Pineville - Ems (not shown to be LR&N). Tremont & Gulf trackage near Winnfield (another road's).
metadata.freight_only_excluded: No LR&N line was freight-only from the start. The Naples route after its last confirmed passenger year (1922) and in any case after the 1928 re-route is not drawn; its freight afterlife is unknown.
metadata.colour_choice: Shreveport and Red River Valley #4A6B8A and Louisiana Railway and Navigation #9C2A4B are new; neither company had a feature in data/ and neither hex was used by any company in data/ on 2026-11-12 (checked programmatically).
known_defects_elsewhere: data/shreveport_railroads.geojson | kcs-southern-belle 'Kansas City Southern: Southern Belle' (#006747): segments 1897-1907 and 1907-1939 draw KCS colour on geometry that south of Shreveport is the ex-S&RRV / LR&N main line (confirmed 2026-11-12: the line passes within 0.3 km of Coushatta, Colfax, Mansura, Simmesport, Gonzales and LaPlace). That track carried S&RRV trains from 1899, LR&N trains 1903-1928/29 (to New Orleans only from 14 Apr 1907) and L&A trains 1929-1939; KCS ran none of it before the Oct 1939 L&A acquisition. The 1907-1939 note's 'through Shreveport-New Orleans passenger service was inaugurated Apr 14 1907' is the LR&N's inauguration. Fix (for the L&A cycle): split at Shreveport; south of it keep KCS from 1939/40 only.

data/shreveport_railroads.geojson | kcs-southern-belle: Rule 2 later-alignment error for every pre-1940 year. Confirmed: the geometry runs Torras (0.6 km) - New Roads (0.6 km) - Port Allen (1.9 km) - Huey P. Long bridge, a route used only from 1940, and passes 9.8 km from Angola and 10.1 km from St. Francisville, so it never draws the Naples/Torras - Angola car ferry and east-bank Angola - Baton Rouge line used 1907-1940. Its geometry_quality says nothing about this.

data/shreveport_railroads.geojson | kcs-southern-belle 1940-1969 segment note: says the Southern Belle and Flying Crow used 'Texas & Pacific track for the Baton Rouge-New Orleans leg'. The T&P detour was Torras Jct - Lobdell up to the Huey P. Long bridge (Fowler table 22); south of Baton Rouge the KCS trains used the ex-LR&N east-bank line (Jan 1952 Official Guide table 2: Gonzales 255.1, La Place 285.7, New Orleans 312.7), which is what the feature's own geometry draws. Text error, not years.

data/shreveport_railroads.geojson | tp-shreveport-new-orleans 'Texas and Pacific: Shreveport – New Orleans' (#8B4513), 1882-1930 and 1930-1971: south of Baton Rouge the geometry is the ex-LR&N east-bank line (confirmed: 0.3 km from Gonzales, 0.8 km from LaPlace, but 16.2 km from Donaldsonville and 7.5 km from Westwego). The T&P's own line was the west bank via Addis, Donaldsonville and Westwego (Fowler table 40); the east-bank track did not exist until 1906. Rests on the file metadata's 2026-08-19 CORRECTION, which repeats the note error above.

data/shreveport_railroads.geojson | tp-shreveport-new-orleans: NOT in the research report, found while confirming the above - north of Alexandria the T&P geometry also lies on the ex-S&RRV / LR&N line (0.0 km from Coushatta, Clarence, Montgomery and Colfax), yet passes 8.1 km from Natchitoches, 10.6 km from Cypress and 4.4 km from Boyce. The T&P (New Orleans Pacific) Shreveport - Alexandria route ran down the west side of the Red River via the Natchitoches area, and the Coushatta - Colfax track was not built until 1898-1902, so 1882-1902 at least are drawn on track that did not yet exist and every year is drawn on another company's railroad. Needs confirmation and a retrace by the T&P owner.

properties.geometry_quality: 45.2 mi traced Shreveport - Bossier City - Elm Grove - Crichton - Coushatta against 44.4 mi documented (Fowler table 14). Fully traced from OpenStreetMap: all of it on the active CPKC (ex-KCS / ex-LR&N) line tagged old_railway_operator=KCS. No straight-line leg. The Red River crossing at Shreveport is drawn on the present KCS bridge; whether it sits exactly on the 1890s Shreveport Bridge & Terminal Co. alignment is not checked. Shreveport end is the city centre (0.4 km from the line), not a located S&RRV station. Main-line pieces were traced as one continuous run and cut at the junction towns, so adjoining features meet exactly.

segments.note: William Edenborn's first road, incorporated 23 Jul 1897 and built south from Shreveport down the east bank of the Red River with local tax subsidies; the 1897 Shreveport subsidy contract bound him to run a daily train arriving in Shreveport in the morning and leaving in the evening (Bossier Banner 23 Sep 1897). The line was 'completed and running to Coushatta' by Oct 1898 (Colfax Chronicle 29 Oct 1898), but 'running' is not proven passenger service, so the drawn start is 1899: the Colfax Chronicle of 24 Nov 1900 describes riding the Red River Valley passenger train north to Star Point, a daylight departure that had been 'the custom for a year past'. Ends 1903 because the S&RRV sold the line to the Louisiana Railway and Navigation Company on 22 Jun 1903 (ICC valuation); the same track continues as the LR&N main line feature. One daily train each way is the subsidy contract's pattern, so headway 1440 is an estimate from it, not a timetable.
sources: Segment-level: start from Colfax Chronicle 24 Nov 1900 p1 ('A Trip Up the Valley', daily train 'for a year past') and 29 Oct 1898 p1; daily-train pattern from Bossier Banner 23 Sep 1897 p2 (subsidy agreement); end from the ICC valuation (sale to LR&N 22 Jun 1903). Chronicling America OCR as read by the research report. Headway and speed are estimates.

properties.geometry_quality: 122.2 mi traced Shreveport - Coushatta - St. Maurice - Alexandria against 122.0 mi documented (Fowler table 14). Identical geometry to the three Shreveport and Red River Valley features joined end to end, fully traced on the active CPKC (ex-KCS) line, old_railway_operator=KCS. No straight-line leg. LATER ALIGNMENT at Alexandria: the Red River crossing is the present CPKC bridge; the 1901 LR&N/S&RRV swing-span (used to Jan 1996) has been dismantled and is not drawn. The Shreveport river crossing is drawn on the present KCS bridge, not checked against the period alignment. Main-line pieces were traced as one continuous run and cut at the junction towns, so adjoining features meet exactly.

segments.note: The Louisiana Railway and Navigation Company, incorporated 22 Jun 1903, bought the S&RRV's completed line Shreveport - Alexandria the same day (ICC). Regular passenger trains Nos. 1 and 2 ran by Nov 1906 (Southern Sentinel, Winnfield, 16 Nov 1906); from Sunday 14 Apr 1907 through daily service ran Shreveport - New Orleans, first train leaving Shreveport at 6:30 a.m. (Southern Sentinel 12 Apr 1907); a 1922 timetable gave Shreveport - New Orleans 15 h 35 min including the ferry. At Shreveport the LR&N used the Kansas City, Shreveport & Gulf Terminal Co.'s station for passengers (ICC). One through train each way (headway 1440) is an estimate; locals are not counted. 1923 is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end: no LR&N timetable after 1923 was found, and the LR&N name ran until the Louisiana and Arkansas lease of 1928 or 1929 (sources differ). The 1924-1928 years are a withheld unknown, not an ending. Do not extend without evidence. After the LR&N the Louisiana and Arkansas ran these trains (Hustler 1932) and from 1939/40 the Kansas City Southern (Southern Belle 1940-1969) - those eras are not drawn here.
sources: Segment-level: start from the ICC valuation (LR&N incorporation and purchase 22 Jun 1903); service from Southern Sentinel 16 Nov 1906 p1, 12 Apr 1907 p1, 19 Apr 1907 p1, 8 May 1908 p7, 31 Jul 1908 p7 (Chronicling America) and the 1922 timetable (friedman.cs.illinois.edu); 1923 end [OPEN] from Fowler table 14/15 (New Orleans Terminal Station '1907>1923', 'Konstanz 1923G'). Headway is an estimate.

The S&RRV had track complete to Mansura by the June 1903 sale (ICC) but no passenger train is proven before the 1904 Official Guide, which shows trains terminating at Big Bend beyond Moreauville (Fowler table 21, 'Big Bend 1904G(tm)') - hence 1904, not 1903. Part of the through Shreveport - New Orleans route from 14 Apr 1907. Headway 1440 is an estimate. 1923 is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end: no LR&N timetable after 1923 was found, and the LR&N name ran until the Louisiana and Arkansas lease of 1928 or 1929 (sources differ). The 1924-1928 years are a withheld unknown, not an ending. Do not extend without evidence.

This is the era-correct pre-1928 route, not the later Simmesport line. Main-line pieces were traced as one continuous run and cut at the junction towns, so adjoining features meet exactly.

segments.note: The original river route east from Moreauville through Willard (Vorhies) and Bordelonville to Big Bend (Sarto), where the 1904 Official Guide shows passenger trains terminating (Fowler table 21, 'Big Bend 1904G(tm)'). From 14 Apr 1907 it carried the through trains on to the Naples ferry incline. Last CONFIRMED year 1922: the 1922 timetable still timed the Naples - Angola transfer-boat crossing. The route was replaced in 1928 by Moreauville - Simmesport - Torras (Wikipedia, Angola Transfer Co.; a local source puts a Simmesport rail bridge about 1915, unresolved), so 1923-1928 are a withheld unknown, not an ending; never draw this route after 1928. What became of the line after the re-route is not established. Headway 1440 is an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: start from Fowler table 21 ('Big Bend 1904G(tm)'); 1922 end [OPEN] from the 1922 timetable (friedman.cs.illinois.edu); 1928 re-route from Wikipedia, Angola Transfer Company. Headway is an estimate.

segments.note: Big Bend (Sarto) - Cordes - Naples, the west-bank incline where Angola Transfer Co. barges took the LR&N's cars through Old River and across the Mississippi to Angola, about 8 miles by water (ICC), 2 h 35 min in 1922. Through Shreveport - New Orleans passenger service, and so passenger trains to Naples, began 14 Apr 1907 (Southern Sentinel 12 Apr 1907). The ferry itself is not drawn. Last CONFIRMED year 1922 (1922 timetable); 1923-1928 are a withheld unknown, not an ending, and the route must not be drawn after 1928, when the Simmesport - Torras route replaced it. Naples was later washed away. Headway 1440 is an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: start from Southern Sentinel 12 Apr 1907 p1 (through service from 14 Apr 1907, Chronicling America); ferry from the ICC valuation; 1922 end [OPEN] from the 1922 timetable (friedman.cs.illinois.edu); 1928 re-route from Wikipedia, Angola Transfer Company. Headway is an estimate.

Fully traced on OpenStreetMap ways tagged old_railway_operator=KCS: abandoned grade (ways 697826720, 102518898, 12631139) from the Angola landing to Port Hudson, then active CPKC track into Baton Rouge. No straight-line leg. The Angola end is hand-pinned at the river end of the mapped abandoned grade (30.972 N, 91.647 W); the incline's exact site is not established. Baton Rouge end is the city centre (1.3 km off the line), not a located LR&N station. The line is DISCONTINUOUS at its north end: nothing is drawn across the Mississippi to Naples (car ferry). This is the era-correct east-bank route, not the post-1940 Huey P. Long bridge / Port Allen route. Main-line pieces were traced as one continuous run and cut at the junction towns, so adjoining features meet exactly.

segments.note: The east-bank line from the Angola ferry incline through Tunica, the Bains area (Bingen, Bruder), St. Francisville (Bayou Sara), Port Hudson, Alsen and Maryland (Konstanz) to Baton Rouge - many stations given German names by Edenborn. Road complete Dec 1906 (ICC); through passenger service from 14 Apr 1907 (Southern Sentinel 12 Apr 1907); a Shreveport - Baton Rouge Pullman special arrived 10:15 a.m. on 18 May 1908. Any local service before Apr 1907 is not established and not drawn. Headway 1440 is an estimate. 1923 is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end: no LR&N timetable after 1923 was found, and the LR&N name ran until the Louisiana and Arkansas lease of 1928 or 1929 (sources differ). The 1924-1928 years are a withheld unknown, not an ending. Do not extend without evidence. The L&A kept using this line with the Torras ferry until the Huey P. Long bridge opened in 1940; that era is not drawn here.
sources: Segment-level: start from Southern Sentinel 12 Apr 1907 p1 and 8 May 1908 (Chronicling America) and the ICC valuation (complete Dec 1906); 1923 end [OPEN] from Fowler table 15 ('Konstanz 1923G'). Headway is an estimate.

properties.geometry_quality: 79.6 mi traced Baton Rouge - Gonzales - LaPlace - Kenner - New Orleans against about 80.1 mi documented (Fowler table 15, 300.4 - 380.5). About 70 mi on the active CPKC (ex-KCS / ex-LR&N) line tagged old_railway_operator=KCS; 8 mi of untagged, IC-tagged and Southern-tagged terminal track from Kenner into Mid-City New Orleans. APPROXIMATED: the New Orleans approach. The 1907-1923 route over 6.20 mi of New Orleans Terminal Co. passenger-only trackage into Terminal Station (Canal and Basin) is not established; the trace follows the shortest surviving path east of Kenner to 29.959 N, 90.095 W, then a STRAIGHT LINE of 1.4 mi to a hand-pinned point at the Basin Street end of the old Carondelet / Lafitte corridor near the Terminal Station site. Treat the last ~5 mi as indicative only. Main-line pieces were traced as one continuous run and cut at the junction towns, so adjoining features meet exactly.

segments.note: The east-bank line Baton Rouge - Prairieville - Gonzales - Sorrento - Gramercy - Garyville - Reserve - LaPlace - Norco - Kenner - New Orleans, into Terminal Station over 6.20 mi of New Orleans Terminal Co. passenger-only trackage (ICC). A Gonzales depot site was advertised Dec 1906 (Donaldsonville Chief 1 Dec 1906) - track, not proven passenger service - so the drawn start is the through-service inauguration of 14 Apr 1907. Headway 1440 is an estimate. 1923 is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end: no LR&N timetable after 1923 was found, and the LR&N name ran until the Louisiana and Arkansas lease of 1928 or 1929 (sources differ). The 1924-1928 years are a withheld unknown, not an ending. Do not extend without evidence. This is the line later used by the L&A and the KCS Southern Belle (OG Jan 1952 table 2: Gonzales 255.1, La Place 285.7, New Orleans 312.7) - not the Texas and Pacific's west-bank route.
sources: Segment-level: start from Southern Sentinel 12 Apr 1907 p1 (Chronicling America); Donaldsonville Chief 1 Dec 1906; terminal trackage from the ICC valuation; 1923 end [OPEN] from Fowler table 15 (New Orleans Terminal Station 1907>1923). Headway is an estimate.

properties.geometry_quality: 27.0 mi traced Aloha - Verda - Lofton - Emden - Atlanta - Whitford - Winnfield against 27.184 mi documented (ICC; Fowler table 18, 92.3 - 119.8). Fully traced on OpenStreetMap ways tagged old_railway_operator=KCS. No straight-line leg apart from the 0.2 mi junction join described below (APPROXIMATED). Checked against the decoys: it does not use the Missouri Pacific Monroe Subdivision (Winnfield - Alexandria) or the L&A's own Hope - Winnfield - Alexandria line. At Aloha the branch's first 0.2 mi is a short straight join from the branch's traced end to the nearest point of the main-line feature, so the two meet.

segments.note: Aloha (on the main line) - Verda - Lofton - Emden - Atlanta - Whitford - Winnfield, 27.184 mi (ICC); partly built by the S&RRV in 1903 and finished by the LR&N. In Nov 1906 LR&N tickets were sold 'at all Agency Stations to Shreveport' for the regular passenger trains Nos. 1 and 2 (Southern Sentinel, Winnfield, 16 Nov 1906; Fowler 'Loftin 1906G'). Double daily service from 14 Apr 1907 (trains 5, 7, 6, 8) connecting at Aloha (Southern Sentinel 12 Apr 1907) - headway 720 is from that, though the Jul 1908 card lists a single No. 4 (Southern Sentinel 31 Jul 1908), so treat it as an estimate. 1908 is the last CONFIRMED year, NOT a known end: the branch's later passenger years and its end are not established. Do not extend without evidence. Not to be confused with the L&A's own Hope - Winnfield - Alexandria line or the Missouri Pacific's Monroe - Winnfield - Alexandria line, both separate railroads.
sources: Segment-level: Southern Sentinel 16 Nov 1906 p1, 12 Apr 1907 p1, 31 Jul 1908 p7 (Chronicling America); Fowler table 18 ('Loftin 1906G'); mileage from the ICC valuation. 1908 end is [OPEN]. Headway is an estimate.

properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (mail.ru mirror) traced with opstrace.py: ways tagged old_railway_operator=KCS / Louisiana and Arkansas costed 1x, untagged rail 1.25x, other named operators 12x; abandoned/historic ways and OpenHistoricalMap fetched for lifted stretches; Douglas-Peucker 8 m, reversals trimmed.
properties.geometry_quality: 178.8 mi traced Waskom - Jefferson - Avinger - Hughes Springs - Daingerfield - Pittsburg - Winnsboro - Sulphur Springs - Greenville - Farmersville - Princeton - McKinney against 181 mi documented McKinney - state line (TSHA). 128.8 mi on OpenStreetMap ways tagged old_railway_operator KCS (the line's later owner) or MKT; 52.4 mi on OpenHistoricalMap ways named for the line's own predecessors, the Sherman, Shreveport and Southern (26.7 mi) and the East Line and Red River (25.7 mi), where OSM has no surviving trackbed; 1.1 mi on an OHM Texas Midland way and 1.7 mi of untagged track and connectors at junctions. No straight-line leg. The west end stops at Waskom town, about 1 mi short of the state line; Waskom - Shreveport over the Illinois Central is not drawn (LR&N of Texas use not confirmed).

segments.note: The Louisiana Railway and Navigation Company of Texas, chartered 27 Mar 1923, began operating 1 Apr 1923 the 181 mi McKinney - Texas/Louisiana state line near Waskom bought from the reorganizing Katy (ex Sherman, Shreveport & Southern / East Line & Red River), through Jefferson, Hughes Springs, Daingerfield, Pittsburg, Winnsboro, Sulphur Springs, Greenville and Farmersville. ANCHOR: 1926 is the single year a source proves LR&N-name passenger service ('In 1926 ... passenger earnings $110,000', TSHA). Service certainly ran wider both ways - very likely 1923-1929 - but no other year is confirmed; do not widen this anchor without evidence. Same owner (Edenborn interests) and same colour as the LR&N. Leased to the L&A 1929, renamed Louisiana, Arkansas and Texas 14 Apr 1930 - not drawn here. Whether the trains ran on into Shreveport over the Illinois Central (ex-VS&P) from the state line is not confirmed, so Waskom - Shreveport is not drawn. Headway 1440 is an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: TSHA, Louisiana Railway and Navigation Company of Texas (1926 passenger earnings; charter and 1 Apr 1923 start); TSHA, Louisiana, Arkansas and Texas Railway (1930 rename, 1939 merger). Headway and speed are estimates.
